newsitem.title: USA: Teacher demands more than apples from students.
newsitem.headline: Teacher demands more than apples from students.

text.p: A high school teacher traded his students good grades and excuses for skipping class in exchange for giving him gifts or allowing him to shoplift at stores where they worked, prosecutors said Thursday.

Douglas Petrovitch, 28, has been indicted by a grand jury in suburban Waukegan, Ill., and was fired from Lake Zurich High School after an investigation turned up at least four students who traded goods for grades and excused absences.
"He taught applied economics, which I suppose is appropriate," assistant Lake County Prosecutor George Strickland said.

In two instances, he persuaded students who worked as cashiers in suburban department stores to charge him around $100 for about $1,000 worth of items, Strickland said. After being nabbed by store security in one shoplifting attempt, Petrovich pleaded guilty last month to theft and paid a $500 fine.

Subsequently other students came forward and described how Petrovich told them they could earn A's or skip class in exchange for providing him a $50 gift certificate at a restaurant or for bringing him lunch, officials said.

A grand jury handed up an indictment in which Petrovich was charged with four counts of official misconduct and two counts of intimidation, all felonies for which he could receive up to five years in prison. He was free pending a bond hearing next week.
